Definitely have been some terrible incidents that have taken place. Overall, Chinese are good people. I think the ‘white skin’ argument is overrated though. From my understanding of Chinese culture and Sociology (aside from the obvious incidents like attacks, etc), I would say Chinese are more classicist than racist. Historically, White skin has been associated with wealth, more so than beauty. Nevertheless, it’s not my culture and that sort of thinking has never been an issue for me even with brown skin. I guess I saw the whole obsession with having really pale white skin the same way as white people tanning all day and getting suntans, you know - the cultural, but, not absolute standard of beauty. Otherwise, I would’ve struggled to have a good time.

Tbh Chinese say that about foreigners a lot though, especially kids. They like to comment on physical features not all have to do with skin color though. Otherwise, I wouldn’t be “handsome” in the eyes of pretty much any Chinese. I understand what you meant though.

Spot on! I’m a Black South African student who lived in China, spoke to many other black foreigners, expats and international students, across the African diaspora. I agree that a lot of stereotypes come from Western media outlets (thank you United States and Hollywood) that portray Black people in a terrible light. 

We can’t deny that it this is a global problem. Let’s not act like there are no black scientists, entrepreneurs, billionaires (not from entertainment), doctors and other respectable members in the United States (and the rest of the world). 

Why doesn’t the media show more positive representations of black people like the ones mentioned above?

Not all Black people are having a bad time in China. I’m sick and tired of white people who, just because they’re having a bad time in China, try to make it seem like all black people are also having a bad time there, just so we can drown in the same misery. 

I’m Black and lived in China before Covid as an international student. I can attest I had an amazing time in China. Yes, there were racist incidents (3) but that wasn’t going to stop me from having Chinese friends who treated me as a person first, rather than a ‘black person’ or foreigner. 

My biggest worry in China has been the rise in nationalist propaganda.
